rejected.title: The power of the medieval Church
card: In medieval Europe, the Catholic Church was the main source of learning. Monks and nuns copied books by hand in monasteries, and the Church ran most schools and early universities.
The Church was also a major authority. Priests, bishops and the Pope guided how people were expected to live and believe.
The Church had its own courts, called Church courts. They judged clergy and cases about matters such as marriage and wills, using Church law.
The Church collected a tax called the tithe, usually a tenth of a person's produce or income. It also owned large areas of land, which made it wealthy.
rejected.remember: The Church shaped learning and authority, and it had its own courts, taxes and land.

a.q: Which of these shows the Church acting as a source of learning in medieval Europe?
opts: Monks copying books by hand in a monastery
Church courts judging a case about a will
Farmers paying a tithe from their harvest
Bishops owning large estates of farmland
a.why: Copying books and running schools is how the Church kept and passed on learning. The courts, the tithe and the land show its authority and wealth, not its role in learning.
a.clue: Which one is about books and knowledge?

b.q: In medieval England, a monk is accused of stealing. A bishop's court tries him under Church law, not the king's court. Which power of the Church does this show?
opts: The Church had its own courts
The Church ran most schools
The Church collected the tithe
The Church owned large areas of land
b.why: The monk is one of the clergy, and he is judged by a court the Church ran, using its own law. A bishop is involved, which can make land or the tithe tempting, but this case is about judging someone, not about wealth.
b.clue: Who heard the case, and whose law did they use?

b.q: In a village in medieval France, a farmer gives the local priest one tenth of his wheat harvest each year. What is this payment called?
opts: The tithe, a Church tax
A Church court fine
A gift of Church land
A fee for copying books
b.why: The tithe was a Church tax, usually a tenth of produce or income. A court fine is a different payment, because it is set by a Church court when someone is judged, not collected each year from everyone.
b.clue: Think of the Church's yearly tax on a tenth of produce.
